skill.name: creating-pull-requests
skill.description: Helps create GitHub pull requests by checking branch state, pushing the branch, and opening a PR with a structured description.
skill.summary: Guides git pre-checks, branch push, GitHub PR creation, and a concise completion report.
skill.author: 1gy

security_audit.summary: The skill is a focused GitHub pull request workflow that declares git and gh Bash usage. Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives, but the PR creation example uses shell substitution and an unescaped title placeholder that can increase shell expansion risk.

remediation.issue: Command substitution in the PR body template
remediation.suggestion: Replace the body command substitution with gh --body-file - and a quoted heredoc, or another method that passes body text without running an inner command.

remediation.issue: Generated PR title is shown as a double-quoted shell placeholder
remediation.suggestion: Document safe quoting for generated titles, or use a variable or gh workflow that avoids inserting untrusted title text directly into a shell command.

content.value_statement: Preparing a pull request requires branch checks, a remote push, and a clear review description. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a consistent GitHub PR workflow.
actual_capabilities: Checks the current branch, working tree status, and commit history against the main branch.
Pushes the current branch to the origin remote with upstream tracking.
Creates a GitHub pull request with a title, summary, and test plan.
Documents optional PR flags for draft mode, base branch, assignee, and labels.
Returns a completion report with the PR URL, title, and target branch.
limitations: Requires git and GitHub CLI to be installed and authenticated.
Assumes the repository uses GitHub and an origin remote.
Does not run tests or verify CI results by itself.
Requires the user or agent to choose accurate summary and test plan content.

use_cases.title: Open a Feature PR
use_cases.description: Create a review-ready pull request after finishing a feature branch and checking local repository state.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team Review
use_cases.description: Standardize PR descriptions so reviewers see clear changes, test coverage, and target branch information.

use_cases.title: Create Draft Workflows
use_cases.description: Open a draft PR early while still capturing summary, test plan, assignee, base branch, and labels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Standard PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a ready branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the creating-pull-requests skill to check the current branch, push it if needed, and create a GitHub pull request with a summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Draft PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the creating-pull-requests skill to create a draft pull request for the current branch. Include a concise summary, open test items, and the target branch.

prompt_templates.title: Target a Specific Base Branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for release or hotfix branches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the creating-pull-requests skill to compare this branch with the project main branch, then create a pull request against the base branch I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Review-Ready PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with richer review context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the creating-pull-requests skill to inspect branch status and recent commits. Draft a reviewer-focused summary, apply requested PR options, and report the final PR URL.

output_examples.input: Create a PR for the current feature branch after checking repository state.
output: Current branch, status, and recent commits checked.
Branch pushed to the origin remote with upstream tracking.
Pull request opened with a summary, test plan, title, target branch, and URL.

output_examples.input: Open a draft PR targeting the develop branch and assign it to me.
output: Draft pull request opened against develop.
Description includes changed areas and review checklist items.
Completion report lists the PR URL, title, and target branch.

output_examples.input: Prepare a PR description from recent branch commits before creating the PR.
output: Commit range reviewed against the configured main branch.
Summary and test plan prepared in the expected format.
PR creation result reported with key review details.

best_practices: Review the branch status and diff before allowing the PR creation command to run.
Keep the PR summary factual and tie each test item to a real verification step.
Confirm the base branch, labels, and assignee before publishing the pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not create a PR from a dirty working tree without explaining the uncommitted changes.
Do not use placeholder summary or test plan text in a published pull request.
Do not target a release or main branch without confirming that branch choice first.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses gh to create the pull request, so GitHub CLI must be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Does it push my branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes pushing the current branch to origin with upstream tracking before creating the PR.

faq.question: Can it create draft pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented options include draft mode for pull requests that are not ready for full review.

faq.question: Can I choose a target branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports a base branch option and asks users to check project guidance for the main branch name.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a test plan section, but test execution must be requested or completed separately.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if local git access and gh authentication already allow the operation. Review the command before publishing private work.
